react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: tryptophan metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + KEGG + WikiPathways) returned Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380) as the top hit with an FDR of 1.46e-15, driven by six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and quinolinic acid). Mummichog's m/z-direct network activity also ranked Tryptophan metabolism first (p=0.0037, overlap 14/15 compounds), confirming this result in a paradigm that operates without annotated IDs. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed hsa00380 at rank 1 (p=1.79e-07) with five overlapping metabolites. The Reactome pathway Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and the WikiPathways Tryptophan metabolism pathway (WP:WP465) further corroborate this signal. The driver metabolites map across two major branches of tryptophan catabolism: the kynurenine arm (quinolinic acid) and the neurotransmitter arm (serotonin-melatonin). The detection of iron (a cofactor for tryptophan hydroxylase) and pyrophosphate (a co-substrate for kinases in these pathways) is biologically coherent. The six core tryptophan-metabolite hits span >857-fold enrichment in the ORA analysis, representing one of the strongest metabolomics signals achievable. This pattern is consistent with a systemic perturbation of tryptophan allocation — a hallmark of inflammatory, neurodevelopmental, or metabolic stress conditions.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a dominant tryptophan-metabolism signal. RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG + WikiPathways + Reactome) reports KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as the top hit with FDR 1.46e-15 and fold enrichment 857.8, driven by six input metabolites. Mummichog's m/z-direct network activity independently confirms the same pathway at p=0.0041 with an overlap of 14 out of 15 compounds. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA returns hsa00380 (equivalent to KEGG:map00380) as the top pathway at p=1.79e-07 with five overlapping metabolites. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-209931 "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" appears as a pathway member hit with three overlapping compounds. WikiPathways WP:WP4210 "Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production" ranks among the top ten hits (FDR 7.30e-08). Mummichog separately links quinolinic acid to the nicotinamide metabolism arm. The six core driver metabolites span both the serotonin/melatonin branch and the kynurenine/quinolinic acid branch of tryptophan catabolism, indicating broad rewiring of tryptophan allocation. L-tryptophan is the entry-point substrate; indoleacetaldehyde and tryptamine are pathway intermediates on the serotonin branch; quinolinic acid sits on the NAD+-biosynthesis branch.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA and Mummichog network analysis converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal in this dataset. RaMP identifies KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit with FDR 1.46e-15 and fold enrichment 857.8, driven by six overlapping metabolites including quinolinic acid, L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. Mummichog independently reports MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top pathway with p=0.00286 and an overlap of 14 out of 15 compounds. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) ranks sixth with FDR 2.81e-08, capturing three overlapping compounds. WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) ranks second with FDR 4.93e-12. The convergent enrichment across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms confirms a robust tryptophan-metabolism perturbation spanning the kynurenine branch (quinolinic acid), the serotonin/melatonin branch (serotonin, melatonin), and upstream intermediates (L-tryptophan, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde).
